$description: One error response per code the Partner API can return. Both SDKs map every case to the same `error_class` and make the same `retryable` decision, so a merchant's `catch` block behaves identically in either language.

$notes.error_class: A language-neutral name. TypeScript exports it as a class; PHP as a class in Aminitrust\Escrow\Errors. Adding a code without adding a mapping must fail a test, not fall through to a generic error.
$notes.retryable: Whether the SDK's own retry loop may repeat the request. This is deliberately narrow: only 429, 5xx and transport failures. See the per-case reasoning.
$notes.message: Never switch on this. It is written for humans and may be reworded in any release.

cases.name: validation_error

error.message: amount_minor must be a multiple of 100

cases.why: Deterministic. The same request will fail the same way forever.

cases.name: unknown_request_property
cases.why: The API rejects unrecognised properties rather than ignoring them. This is what a client running ahead of the server looks like - deploy the backend first.

error.message: this transaction cannot be shipped before it is funded

cases.name: unauthorized
cases.why: Missing, malformed, unknown, expired and wrong-mode keys all return this identical body on purpose, so the response cannot be used to probe for valid keys. The SDK must not try to infer which it was.

cases.name: insufficient_scope

error.message: this key lacks the transactions:write scope

cases.why: A distinct code from FORBIDDEN because the fixes differ: this one is solved by issuing a key with more scopes, the other is not solved by anything the merchant can do.

cases.name: not_found
cases.why: Also returned for an object belonging to another partner, or to the other mode. A live key asking about a test transaction gets 404, not 403, so the response cannot confirm an id exists.

cases.name: conflict_in_flight

error.message: a request with this idempotency key is still in progress

cases.why: Safe to repeat after a wait, but the SDK does not do it automatically. A plain CONFLICT also covers a duplicate partner_reference, and the two are distinguishable only by message - which nothing may switch on. Auto-retrying would quietly paper over a duplicate-order bug, so this is handed to the caller.

cases.name: idempotency_conflict

error.message: this Idempotency-Key was used for a different request

cases.why: Retrying can only fail again: the key is bound to a different body. The fix is a new key, which means the caller reused one for two logical requests.

error.message: a released transaction cannot be refunded

cases.name: rate_limited
cases.why: The only 4xx the SDK retries. Retry-After is authoritative when present; the backoff schedule is the fallback, not an override.

error.message: insufficient balance to cover this refund
the payment provider is not responding

cases.name: internal
cases.why: Retried with the same Idempotency-Key, which is what makes repeating a money-moving request safe. A 5xx also deletes the server's idempotency record, so the retry genuinely re-executes rather than replaying a failure.

cases.name: unparseable_body
cases.why: A proxy or load balancer answering instead of the API. There is no error envelope to read, and an SDK that assumes one throws a JSON parse error that tells the merchant nothing about what happened.
